results.result: The authors developed HepG4-seq, a novel method for mapping native G4s in living cells based on hemin-induced proximal biotinylation. The method uses physiological hemin concentrations (25 µM) to activate G4-hemin peroxidase activity, which biotinylates G4s and proximal DNA using biotin-aniline. HepG4-seq identified 6,799 consensus G4 peaks in HEK293 cells under basal conditions and 77,003 peaks after helicase inhibition, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity with minimal perturbation of native G4 folding.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C25, C32, C122-C123, and C136-C140 collectively establish HepG4-seq as a valid method. The experimental data (C19-C25) show specific biotinylation dependent on hemin and Bio-An, good overlap with PQS predictions, and enrichment of G-rich motifs. Control experiments (C20) demonstrate minimal perturbation of native G4s. The method's sensitivity is validated by detecting dynamic changes after helicase inhibition (C28-C32). The technical foundation is well-supported by prior work on G4-hemin complexes and proximity labeling.

results.result: The authors developed HBD-seq, an optimized method for mapping native R-loops using the HBD domain of RNase H1. HBD-seq identified 42,488 consensus R-loop peaks in HEK293 cells with high signal-to-noise ratio, and signals were dramatically diminished by RNase treatment, demonstrating specificity for R-loops.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C17, C33-C34, and C147-C148 establish HBD-seq as a valid method. The experimental data (C33-C34) show robust peak detection with appropriate negative controls (RNase treatment). The method builds on established prior work (C16-C17, C148) using the HBD domain for R-loop recognition. The optimization to avoid GST-fusion protein aggregation issues (C147) is well-justified.

results.result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops exhibit cell type-specific distributions. In HEK293 cells, 5,030 co-localized peaks were identified (73.8% at promoters/5'UTR/exon1/intron1), while mESCs showed 68,482 peaks with different distribution (34.2% at promoters/exon1/intron1, 25.9% intergenic). mESCs showed approximately 10-fold more co-localized peaks than HEK293 cells, demonstrating dramatic cell type-dependent variation.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C38, C44-C48, and C115, C124-C125 demonstrate cell type-specific co-localization patterns. The data show clear quantitative differences in peak numbers and genomic distributions between cell types. The metagene analyses (C37, C49) and motif enrichment (C38, C50) provide consistent supporting evidence. The ~10-fold difference between cell types (C125) is substantial and well-documented.

results.result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops are associated with transcriptionally active genes and regulate their expression. In both HEK293 cells and mESCs, genes associated with co-localized G4s and R-loops showed significantly higher RNA levels than all genes or genes associated with G4s or R-loops alone (Mann-Whitney test p<2.2E-16). Inhibition of G4-resolving helicases BLM or WRN led to hundreds of genes with altered expression, enriched in cell cycle regulation, DNA metabolic processes, and DNA damage response.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C43, C51-C52, and C116, C134-C135 establish transcriptional regulatory roles. The RNA-seq data (C39, C51) with statistical support demonstrate higher expression of co-localized peak-associated genes. The helicase inhibition experiments (C41-C43) provide functional evidence linking G4 accumulation to transcriptional changes. The GO enrichment analyses (C43) are consistent with known G4/R-loop functions. The localization near TSS (C40, C52) supports regulatory roles.

results.result: In mESCs, co-localized G4s and R-loops are enriched at active promoters (18,496 peaks) and active enhancers (15,787 peaks), overlapping with active chromatin marks (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me1) and RNA polymerase II. At active promoters, co-localized peaks show high G4 and R-loop signals with enrichment of H3K4me3, H3K27ac, and RNAP, suggesting involvement with promoter-associated nascent RNAs. At active enhancers, peaks overlap with H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K4me3, and RNAP, suggesting potential involvement of enhancer RNAs (eRNAs).
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C65 and C142-C144 establish the chromatin context of co-localized peaks. The ChIP-seq overlap data (C54, C58, C62-C64) demonstrate clear associations with active chromatin states. The classification into promoter and enhancer types (C55-C57, C142-C143) follows established definitions. The inference about nascent RNAs (C59) and eRNAs (C65, C144) is reasonable given the RNAP co-localization, though direct evidence for RNA involvement is limited.

results.result: Dhx9 is a key regulator of co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs. Loss of Dhx9 resulted in significant changes in G4 and R-loop levels at thousands of co-localized sites, with 1,647 genes up-regulated and 1,916 genes down-regulated. Hundreds of G4-, R-loop-, and co-localized G4&R-loop-associated genes showed differential expression. GO analysis revealed enrichment in processes related to cell differentiation, embryonic development, and pattern specification.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C74, C119-C120 establish Dhx9's regulatory role. The knockout experiments (C69-C73) provide clear functional evidence with appropriate controls. The RNA-seq data (C72-C73) demonstrate transcriptional consequences. The GO enrichment (C74) is consistent with known Dhx9 functions (C75-C77). However, C70 notes that only a small proportion showed simultaneous G4 and R-loop changes, suggesting complex regulation that may involve other factors.

results.result: Dhx9 directly binds to the majority of co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs. Dhx9 CUT&Tag identified 54,982 binding peaks, with 65.5% overlapping 69.9% of co-localized G4s and R-loops. Among Dhx9-bound co-localized peaks, 6,171 showed differential signals in dhx9KO cells (1,382 up-regulated, 4,789 down-regulated), accounting for 50-75% of all differential co-localized peaks. These Dhx9-bound differential peaks were linked to 852 genes with altered expression, enriched in embryonic development and differentiation processes. Key stem cell regulators including Nanog, Lin28a, Bmp4, Wnt8a, Gata2, and Lef1 were identified as direct Dhx9 targets.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C90 and C128-C132 establish direct Dhx9 binding and regulation. The CUT&Tag data (C81-C83) demonstrate genome-wide binding with appropriate motif enrichment. The comparison between WT and dhx9KO (C84-C87) identifies direct targets. The observation that only ~8.5% of Dhx9-bound peaks show differential signals (C129) suggests redundancy (C130), supported by evidence of other helicase expression changes (C131-C132). The identification of specific target genes (C89) provides biological context.

results.result: Loss of Dhx9 impairs self-renewal and pluripotency of mESCs. dhx9KO mESCs showed decreased RNA and protein levels of Lin28a and Oct4, while Nanog RNA increased but protein decreased. dhx9KO cells exhibited modest S-phase arrest, significantly reduced proliferation, and impaired embryoid body formation with altered expression of all three germ lineage markers tested.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C100 and C121 demonstrate functional consequences of Dhx9 loss. The qRT-PCR (C91), western blot (C92-C93), and immunofluorescence (C94) data consistently show altered pluripotency factor levels. The cell cycle (C96), proliferation (C97), and EB differentiation (C98-C99) assays provide multiple lines of functional evidence. The discordance between Nanog RNA and protein (C93) suggests post-transcriptional regulation, which is appropriately noted. The results are consistent with prior work on Dhx9 knockout lethality (C75-C77).

results.result: Inhibition of G4-resolving helicases BLM or WRN with small molecules ML216 or NSC617145 dramatically increases native G4 levels. Treatment resulted in ~70,000 new G4 peaks detected by HepG4-seq (from 6,799 to 77,003 total peaks), with significantly increased G4 signals (Mann-Whitney test p<2.2E-16). This accumulation led to differential expression of hundreds of genes enriched in cell cycle, DNA metabolism, and DNA damage response processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C31, C117-C118 demonstrate dynamic G4 regulation. The helicase inhibitor experiments (C27-C31) provide strong evidence for G4 accumulation with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. The ~10-fold increase in peaks (C29-C30) is substantial. The transcriptional consequences (C118) are consistent with known G4 functions. However, the specificity of the inhibitors (C27) relies on prior work, and potential off-target effects are not discussed.

results.result: Comparison of HepG4-seq with BG4 CUT&Tag reveals complementary detection of G4s. 80% of HepG4-seq peaks in HEK293 cells and 71% in mESCs overlap with BG4 peaks, but BG4 CUT&Tag identified many more peaks (70,954 in HEK293, 103,303 in mESCs). HepG4-seq peaks show sharper resolution around PQS centers than BG4 peaks. Signal intensity differences between cell types may reflect G4 conformation dynamics, as parallel G4s show higher peroxidase activity than anti-parallel G4s.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C106 provide methodological comparison. The overlap analysis (C101-C102) shows substantial but incomplete concordance between methods. The observation of sharper HepG4-seq peaks (C103) suggests better resolution. The interpretation of signal intensity differences as reflecting conformation (C106) is reasonable given prior work (C105), but remains speculative without direct conformation measurements. The suggestion that BG4 may promote G4 folding (C102-C103) is plausible but not definitively proven.

results.result: Comparison of HBD-seq with other R-loop mapping methods shows improved performance. HBD-seq and S9.6 CUT&Tag identified similar peak numbers (125,311 vs 154,993) with 45,989 HBD-seq peaks overlapping 88,036 S9.6 peaks. HBD-seq showed stronger signal intensities and sharper peaks than MapR and GST-2xHBD CUT&Tag. However, HBD-seq generated ~80,000 extra peaks compared to S9.6 CUT&Tag, suggesting differences in detection sensitivity or specificity.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C114 provide methodological validation. The comparisons with S9.6 CUT&Tag (C107-C109) and other HBD-based methods (C112-C114) show reasonable concordance with improved signal quality. The observation of extra HBD-seq peaks (C111) raises questions about specificity versus sensitivity that are acknowledged but not fully resolved. The interpretation that protein status affects mapping (C111) is reasonable given known issues with GST-fusion proteins (C147).

results.result: The most enriched motif in mESC co-localized G4s and R-loops matches the CTCF ChIP-seq motif, suggesting potential modulation of CTCF binding. This is consistent with prior work showing CTCF-bound regions are enriched for both R-loops and G4s.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C127 suggest a connection to CTCF binding. While the motif match (C127) is interesting and consistent with prior work (C126), this is purely correlative. No functional experiments test CTCF binding or activity in relation to co-localized G4s and R-loops. The inference about modulation of CTCF binding requires additional validation.

results.result: Comprehensive mechanistic study of G4 and R-loop interplay is difficult due to redundancy and compensatory roles of regulators.
results.evaluation: Claim C133 is supported by the observation that only a fraction of Dhx9-bound peaks show changes upon Dhx9 loss (C129-C130), and that loss of Dhx9 alters expression of 30 other helicases/regulators (C131-C132). This demonstrates the complexity of the regulatory network, though it is more of a discussion point than a primary result.

results.result: HepG4-seq is a novel antibody-free method for mapping native G4s in living cells. The method uses hemin-induced proximal biotinylation of G4s and was validated by showing specific biotinylation signals, minimal effect on G4 folding, identification of 6,799 consensus peaks in HEK293 cells, overlap with predicted G4-forming sequences, and detection of dynamic G4s upon helicase inhibition.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge HepG4-seq as 'a useful antibody-free method to map G-quadruplexes' and note 'the development and optimization of HepG4-seq...offer novel methods to map native G4s.' While one reviewer states the comparison to existing datasets 'does not unequivocally demonstrate the superiority,' the method itself and its basic functionality are accepted.

results.result: HBD-seq is an optimized method for mapping native R-loops that revealed 42,488 consensus peaks with high signal-to-noise ratio in HEK293 cells, with signals dramatically diminished by RNase treatment.
results.evaluation: Reviewers express concerns about HBD-seq specificity. One reviewer states 'The sensitivity of the HBD-seq signals to a combination of RNase A and RNase H does not demonstrate that HBD-seq specifically reports the presence of RNA:DNA hybrids' and notes 'Legitimate concerns regarding the specificity of the Cut&Tag signals were not addressed.' Another reviewer questions whether 'HBD-seq did not perform satisfactorily and its binding specificity was questionable.'

results.result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops were identified in HEK293 cells (5,030 peaks) and mESCs (68,482 peaks), showing cell-type-specific distribution patterns. In HEK293 cells, 73.8% localized at promoters, 5'UTR, exon1, and intron1, while in mESCs the distribution was more diverse with enrichment at active promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study 'provides extensive data on the distribution of G4s and R-loops, highlighting their co-localization in human and mouse cells' and that it 'identified dynamic, cell-type-specific distributions of co-localized G4s and R-loops.' The datasets are described as 'a good starting point for future functional studies,' indicating acceptance of the descriptive findings.

results.result: Inhibition of helicases BLM or WRN with small molecules resulted in significant accumulation of G4s and differential expression of hundreds of genes linked to co-localized G4s and R-loops, with enrichment in processes related to cell cycle, DNA metabolism, and DNA damage response.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not raise specific concerns about these findings. The data on helicase inhibition effects are part of the accepted descriptive characterization of G4 dynamics, though reviewers note the work 'remains primarily descriptive.'

results.result: Co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs overlap with active chromatin markers (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K36me3, H3K4me1) and RNAP, with distinct patterns at active promoters (18,496 peaks), bivalent promoters, active enhancers (15,787 peaks), poised enhancers, and unmarked enhancers.
results.evaluation: These chromatin mark associations are part of the accepted descriptive characterization. Reviewers acknowledge the study 'provides extensive data on the distribution of G4s and R-loops' without challenging these specific chromatin overlap findings.

results.result: Dhx9 is a key regulator of co-localized G4s and R-loops in mESCs. Loss of Dhx9 resulted in differential G4s and R-loops signals, with 65.5% of Dhx9 binding peaks overlapping with co-localized G4s and R-loops. Dhx9-bound differential peaks were linked to 852 genes with altered expression enriched in developmental processes, including key regulators like Nanog, Lin28a, Bmp4, Wnt8a, Gata2, and Lef1.
results.evaluation: The editor notes 'the strength of the evidence that DHX9 interferes with the ability of mESCs to differentiate by regulating directly the stability of either G4s or R-loops has been improved compared to a previous version, it is still incomplete.' Reviewers acknowledge 'the study consolidates the role of Dhx9 in modulating these structures' but express that 'the authors provide limited mechanistic insight into the major regulator of co-localized G4s and R-loops, helicase Dhx9.'

results.result: Loss of Dhx9 impaired the self-renewal and pluripotency of mESCs, as evidenced by altered expression of pluripotency markers (Lin28a, Oct4, Nanog), modest S-phase arrest, attenuated proliferation, and defects in embryoid body differentiation with differential expression of germ lineage markers.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge that the study 'reveals that the helicase Dhx9 can affect the self-renewal and differentiation capacities of mESCs' and 'explores its impact on mESC self-renewal and differentiation.' While mechanistic details are questioned, the phenotypic observations themselves are accepted.

results.result: Comparison of HepG4-seq with BG4 CUT&Tag showed 80% and 71% overlap in HEK293 cells and mESCs respectively. HepG4-seq peaks exhibited sharper shape and better resolution around PQS centers than BG4 CUT&Tag, with signal intensity differences between cell types possibly reflecting G4 conformation dynamics.
results.evaluation: One reviewer notes 'the comparison between the novel methods and existing ones is an important addition,' but another states 'The new Figure 9 comparing HepG4-seq to existing datasets does not unequivocally demonstrate the superiority of the Hemin-based strategy to map G4s.' The comparison data are acknowledged but their interpretation regarding method superiority remains contested.

results.result: Comparison of HBD-seq with S9.6 CUT&Tag and other R-loop mapping methods (MapR, GST-2xHBD CUT&Tag) showed similar peak numbers but HBD-seq generated ~80,000 extra peaks compared to S9.6 CUT&Tag and exhibited stronger signal intensities and sharper peak shapes than MapR and GST-2xHBD CUT&Tag.
results.evaluation: While one reviewer acknowledges 'the comparison between the novel methods and existing ones is an important addition,' concerns about HBD-seq specificity persist. One reviewer notes 'the reliability and accuracy of these methods are still debatable' and questions whether HBD-seq 'did not perform satisfactorily.' The comparison data are presented but do not resolve underlying specificity concerns.

results.result: HepG4-seq is capable of robustly and specifically capturing native G4s with high sensitivity, as demonstrated by detection of 6,799 peaks under wild-type conditions and 77,003 peaks with helicase inhibition.
results.evaluation: Reviewers describe HepG4-seq as 'a useful antibody-free method' and acknowledge 'the development and optimization of HepG4-seq...offer novel methods to map native G4s.' The basic capability and sensitivity of the method are accepted, though superiority claims are questioned.

results.result: Endogenous co-localized G4s and R-loops are prevalently present in regulatory regions of active genes and are involved in transcriptional regulation of their linked genes.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the study shows co-localized structures 'predominantly localize at active promoters and enhancers of transcriptionally active genes' and accept the descriptive characterization, though they note the work 'remains primarily descriptive' and 'does not substantially add to existing publications.'

results.result: Only a fraction (4,060 of 47,857) of Dhx9-bound co-localized G4s and R-loops displayed differential signals upon Dhx9 loss, suggesting redundant regulators exist. Loss of Dhx9 altered expression of 30 helicases/regulators, half of which form physical interaction networks, highlighting the complexity and redundancy of G4 and R-loop regulation.
results.evaluation: These findings on regulatory complexity and redundancy are accepted as part of the descriptive characterization. Reviewers acknowledge the study addresses 'the interplay between G-quadruplexes (G4s) and R-loops' and the complexity of their regulation, though they note limited mechanistic insight.

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate HepG4-seq method validation (C19-C25, C32). OpenEval finds the method well-supported with comprehensive experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept it as 'a useful antibody-free method' but one reviewer notes the comparison to existing datasets 'does not unequivocally demonstrate superiority.' Agreement on basic functionality, disagreement on superiority claims.

Both address HepG4-seq sensitivity and capability (C122-C123). OpenEval emphasizes validation through helicase inhibition experiments. Peer reviewers acknowledge the method as 'useful' and 'novel' for mapping native G4s, accepting basic capability though questioning superiority claims.

Both evaluate HBD-seq method validation (C33-C34). OpenEval finds the method well-supported with robust peak detection and appropriate controls.
